_comment: Hand-verified interior-seam trim points for the 9 Surahs that decideTwoPageMerge() (generate-surah-pdfs.mjs, PDF-CONTENT.md §4b) composes from 2 scanned pages onto 1 output page. Bug this fixes: the merge originally used FRAME_TOP_DFT/FRAME_BOTTOM_DFT (each source page's own natural print-template margin) for whichever side of the seam ISN'T a real Surah-boundary crop — but that natural margin sits INSIDE that page's own ornamental border band (the same decorative box used for a real Surah opening/closing), so the merged output showed a full closing border at the bottom of page 1's region immediately followed by a full opening border at the top of page 2's region: a fake 'Surah ended here' seam in the middle of ONE continuing Surah (confirmed both by hand-inspecting the source scans and by rendering the actual generated output through a real browser pdf.js/Canvas pipeline — the Node-canvas preview tool used elsewhere in this pipeline, scripts/pdf/render-preview.mjs, cannot be trusted for this: it disables context.clip() for an unrelated reason, which also defeats embedPage's own required BBox clip, so it either shows blank output or exactly this kind of false bleed-through — see PDF-CONTENT.md §6a). The fix: trim each side to the genuinely blank gap between the last/first real content and that page's own border band, so the seam reads as plain inter-line whitespace (plus generate-surah-pdfs.mjs's existing MERGE_GAP_PT) with no border at all — exactly the 'no divider, just breathing room' intent §4b's own comment already described but the implementation didn't actually achieve for the two seam-adjacent frame edges.
_measurement: Both DFT values (distance in PDF points from the TOP of the page) were read off a per-row ink-density scan of the raw, watermark-stripped source page (never the generated/merged output, for the reason above) in the 0.06-0.94 x-fraction band (excluding the frame's own vertical side borders): innerBottomDFT is the blank row nearest the bottom of the FIRST page's region1, just above where that page's own border band begins; innerTopDFT is the blank row nearest the top of the SECOND page's region2, just below where that page's own border band ends. Every one of the 9 pairs below was measured directly (not assumed from a shared constant) even though the top-side value clusters tightly at 86 across all of them, matching this print template's consistent border-band height (PDF-CONTENT.md §4b's own FRAME_TOP_DFT/FRAME_BOTTOM_DFT measurement) — kept per-entry rather than hardcoded once, so a future re-verification (source PDFs replaced) re-checks every one explicitly rather than trusting an assumed shared constant, per this pipeline's established practice (surah-boundary-crops.json's own §4a note).
